actionable_steps.citation: Discrimination Is The Means To Selfrealisation — Sri Sathya Sai Speaks, Vol 40 (2007), 2007-08-22
actionable_steps.step: Before you undertake any task, enquire: is this good or bad, is this right or wrong?

actionable_steps.citation: Sabko sanmathi — Sri Sathya Sai Speaks, Vol 12 (1973 - 74), 1973-03-30
actionable_steps.step: Judge each idea in the Supreme Court of viveka, and treat its ruling as inviolable.

actionable_steps.citation: Discrimination Is The Means To Selfrealisation — Sri Sathya Sai Speaks, Vol 40 (2007), 2007-08-22
actionable_steps.step: Adopt fundamental discrimination — choose what is beneficial to society at large, not merely what suits your self-interest.

actionable_steps.citation: Sustained saadhana — Sri Sathya Sai Speaks, Vol 5 (1965)
actionable_steps.step: Keep your buddhi sharp, so that it may cut the mind like a diamond and convert it into a blaze of light.

actionable_steps.citation: Cherish the sweetness of sacrifice — Sri Sathya Sai Speaks, Vol 27 (1994), 1994-07-03
actionable_steps.step: Know what to say, when and to whom — and how to behave towards elders, friends, and different kinds of people.

definition.citation: Discrimination Is The Means To Selfrealisation — Sri Sathya Sai Speaks, Vol 40 (2007), 2007-08-22
definition.quote: It is enough if you have discrimination. Before you undertake any task, always enquire, "Is this good or bad, is this right or wrong?" You will come up in life if you develop this one quality in you.

discourses.citation: Bhakthi, stage by stage — Sri Sathya Sai Speaks, Vol 15 (1981 - 82), 1982-01-23
discourses.quote: 'Panda' means viveka or discrimination. One who has viveka is Panditha. This viveka is of two types: one is worldly or Bhouthika, and the other is spiritual or Adhyathmika.

discourses.citation: Cherish the sweetness of sacrifice — Sri Sathya Sai Speaks, Vol 27 (1994), 1994-07-03
discourses.quote: Jnana is the capacity to discriminate between right and wrong, the permanent and the transient. … A real human being has to have this power of discrimination.

discourses.citation: How old are you really? — Sri Sathya Sai Speaks, Vol 4 (1964), 1964-10-10
discourses.quote: Moksha is the recognition of the truth; but, though it is so simple, it required the cultivation of viveka, vairagya and vichakshana (discrimination, detachment and ability), to know the Truth and escape from the temptation to hug falsehood.

discourses.citation: The Four Gates — Sri Sathya Sai Speaks, Vol 20 (1987), 1987-02-19
discourses.quote: The second gate that you have to pass through is Vicharana (Enquiry) - the process of discriminating between right and wrong, good and evil, the transient and the eternal.

make_it_real: Pause before every choice today and ask Swami's question: is this good or bad, right or wrong?
title: Discrimination (Viveka)

vahinis.quote: Discrimination is the faculty that enables us to distinguish good from bad and confers upon us the ability to decide how much importance to give to various aspects in a given situation. … Without discrimination, one cannot pursue the right path.

An ethical life is based upon discrimination between truth and falsehood. Just as the pearl is retained while the shell is discarded, the essence that is truth must be accepted and the nonessential rejected.
